pharm: Binds retinoic acid receptors to induce terminal differentiation and apoptosis of leukemic promyelocytes carrying the PML/RARalpha fusion.
quick: 45 mg/m2/day orally in two divided doses (22.5 mg/m2 twice daily)
Take with a meal; swallow capsule whole
Avoid; do not breastfeed during and after treatment
Avoid; adds hepatotoxicity and lipid effects
CBC, coagulation, LFTs, lipids, differentiation syndrome
summary: Oral tretinoin (all-trans retinoic acid) induces remission in acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) bearing the t(15;17) translocation or PML/RARalpha fusion. It carries a boxed warning for embryo-fetal toxicity and for differentiation syndrome (retinoic acid syndrome), which is potentially fatal and occurs in about 26% of treated patients. Treatment requires close hematologic, coagulation, lipid, and liver monitoring, and strict contraception.
indications: Induction of remission in adults and pediatric patients >=1 year with acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL) characterized by t(15;17) translocation or PML/RARalpha gene expression, who are refractory to or relapsed from anthracycline chemotherapy, or for whom anthracycline-based chemotherapy is contraindicated

dosage.d: 45 mg/m2/day in two evenly divided doses (22.5 mg/m2 twice daily)
Discontinue 30 days after complete remission or after 90 days of treatment, whichever comes first
Add cytoreductive chemotherapy (anthracycline if not contraindicated, or hydroxyurea) as clinically indicated

admin: Take capsules with a meal; swallow whole with water - do not chew, dissolve, or open
Verify a negative pregnancy test in females of reproductive potential before starting
At first signs of differentiation syndrome, start high-dose corticosteroids and hemodynamic monitoring immediately
If vomiting occurs after a dose, do not repeat it; continue with the next scheduled dose
Monitor white blood cell count closely during induction
moa: In APL, the t(15;17) translocation produces a PML/RARalpha fusion protein that blocks myeloid differentiation. Pharmacologic concentrations of all-trans retinoic acid bind the retinoic acid receptor, overcome the maturation block, and induce terminal differentiation and subsequent apoptosis of the leukemic promyelocytes, restoring normal hematopoiesis. It does not directly kill the cells via cytotoxic mechanisms.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to tretinoin, its components, or other retinoids

preg: Boxed warning: tretinoin can cause embryo-fetal loss and severe malformations. It is contraindicated in pregnancy. Females of reproductive potential must have a negative pregnancy test before starting and use two effective contraceptive methods during and for 1 month after the last dose; males with partners of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and for 1 week after the last dose.
lact: It is not known whether tretinoin is excreted in human milk; because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the breastfed infant, do not breastfeed during treatment.
renal: No specific renal dosing data are provided; use with caution and monitor for toxicity in renal impairment.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity has occurred; monitor liver function tests at baseline and during treatment and reduce or interrupt therapy as clinically indicated for significant elevations.

major: Strong CYP enzyme inducers/inhibitors (tretinoin is CYP-metabolized; altered exposure)
Antifibrinolytic agents (e.g., tranexamic/aminocaproic acid) - reports of fatal thrombosis when combined
moderate: Other retinoids / vitamin A (additive hypervitaminosis A toxicity)
Drugs causing intracranial hypertension (e.g., tetracyclines) - additive pseudotumor cerebri
Hormonal contraceptives (efficacy may be affected; use additional non-hormonal method)
interactions.food: Take with a meal to improve absorption.
interactions.diagnostics: May markedly elevate serum triglycerides, cholesterol, and liver enzymes.

emergency: Differentiation syndrome with respiratory distress / multi-organ failure

monitoring: Signs/symptoms of differentiation syndrome (fever, dyspnea, weight gain, edema, infiltrates, effusions)
Complete blood count with differential and WBC
Pregnancy testing in females of reproductive potential
counsel: This medicine can cause severe birth defects - strict contraception is mandatory before, during, and after treatment
Report fever, shortness of breath, weight gain, or swelling immediately - these can signal a serious reaction
Headache, dry skin and lips, and bone pain are common
Take capsules whole with a meal; do not open or chew them
Avoid vitamin A supplements and alcohol during treatment
pk: Hematologic response over days to weeks
Terminal ~0.5-2 hours; levels decline with continued dosing (autoinduction)
Store at 20-25 C; protect from light
pearls: Two boxed warnings: embryo-fetal toxicity and differentiation syndrome (occurs in ~26%, can be fatal)
First sign of differentiation syndrome - start high-dose dexamethasone immediately, do not wait
Confirm t(15;17)/PML-RARalpha; discontinue if not present
Rising WBC predicts differentiation syndrome - add cytoreduction as needed
APL coagulopathy/DIC is a major early cause of death - support coagulation aggressively
missed: Do not take a missed dose unless it is more than 10 hours until the next scheduled dose; otherwise skip it and resume the normal schedule. Do not double up.
overdose: Overdose reflects acute hypervitaminosis A: headache, nausea/vomiting, lethargy, ataxia, and skin/mucosal effects. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively. Effects are usually transient and reversible.
